office_does: The assessor values property for taxation, keeps assessments fair and equitable, and explains values and appeal rights to property owners.
race_blurb: Assessor Veronica Rodriguez, in the office since 2015 and Assessor since a 2019 appointment, faces career appraiser and deputy assessor Curtis Templin; both prefer the Republican Party. Templin led the primary 1,295 to 1,039 and argues the office has lacked seasoned professional knowledge; Rodriguez cites timely assessments and compliance with state standards.

candidates.summary: Adams County Assessor since a 2019 appointment, elected in 2022, after starting in the office in 2015; seeking a second term on her record.
highlights: In the Assessor's Office since 2015; appointed Assessor in 2019, elected unopposed in 2022 [S2][S3]
Cites timely assessments, better communication with owners and compliance with state assessment standards [S1]
The State Auditor's 2024 county accountability audit, which examined property tax valuations, reported no findings [S5]

experience.basis: Sitting Assessor with 11 years in the office who asks voters for continued support on her record.

candidates.summary: Appraiser, appraiser analyst and deputy county assessor for more than 11 years, and a fourth-generation Adams County farmer near Ritzville; seeking his first elected office.
highlights: Says recent years show 'the difficulties of operating without a foundation of seasoned professional knowledge' [S1]
Would improve response times, ensure equitable assessments and explain values and appeals clearly [S1]
Accredited appraiser in Adams and Lincoln counties; on an IAAO chapter education committee [S1]

experience.basis: First run for office, framed as a change in how the office is run, but built on a long appraisal and deputy-assessor career rather than an outsider profile.
